Rain, snow, sleet and hail.

lessons.try: Build a rain gauge from a bottle.

learn: Wind is moving air.
A wind vane shows direction. An anemometer measures speed.
Wind is named for where it comes from.
lessons.try: Make a wind vane.

learn: Clouds are tiny water drops or ice crystals.
Cumulus are puffy. Stratus are flat layers. Cirrus are wispy and high.
Dark cumulonimbus clouds bring storms.
lessons.try: Identify clouds in the sky this week.

learn: Record weather in a table each day.
Columns: date, temperature, precipitation, wind, clouds.
Tables show patterns.
check: Which belongs in a weather table?
lessons.try: Keep a two-week weather table.

learn: Bar graphs show rainfall per month.
Line graphs show temperature changes.
Graphs help us compare.
check: Bar graphs can show ___ per month.
lessons.try: Graph a month of temperatures.

learn: Seasons are patterns of weather across the year.
Summer is warm; winter is cold.
Seasons happen because Earth is tilted.
lessons.try: Make a seasons wheel.

learn: Climate is the usual weather of a place over many years.
Weather is today; climate is the long pattern.
Deserts have dry climates. Rainforests have wet ones.
lessons.try: Compare weather and climate on a chart.

learn: Polar zones are cold. Tropical zones near the equator are hot.
Temperate zones have four seasons.
Where you live affects your climate.
lessons.try: Colour climate zones on a world map.

learn: Much of Arizona has a hot, dry desert climate.
Summer monsoons bring sudden storms.
Mountains in the north are cooler and snowy.
check: Much of Arizona has a ___ climate.
lessons.try: Compare Phoenix and Flagstaff weather.

learn: Weather is now. Climate is the long-term pattern.
Tools measure temperature, rain and wind.
Data and graphs show patterns.
lessons.try: Give a weather report to the class.

learn: Natural hazards are events in nature that can cause harm.
Hurricanes bring strong winds and heavy rain. Tornadoes are spinning columns of air. Floods happen when water overflows onto land.
Forecasts and warnings give people time to prepare.
check: A spinning column of air is a...
What gives people time to prepare?
lessons.try: Find out which natural hazards are common where you live.

learn: Earthquakes are sudden shaking of the ground.
Volcanoes can erupt with lava, ash and gas.
Landslides happen when soil and rock slide down a slope.
check: What do you do in an earthquake?
Stand in a doorway on a high floor
Soil and rock slide down a slope
lessons.try: Learn "Drop, Cover and Hold On" for earthquakes.

learn: Engineers design solutions to reduce the harm of hazards.
Levees and flood walls hold back water. Lightning rods protect buildings. Strong frames help buildings survive earthquakes.
Families can prepare an emergency kit with water, food, a flashlight and a first-aid kit.
lessons.try: Make a checklist for a family emergency kit.

learn: Natural hazards are natural events that can harm people.
Storms, floods, earthquakes, wildfires and droughts.
We can't stop them, but we can prepare.
lessons.try: List hazards that happen near you.

learn: Thunderstorms bring lightning, heavy rain and wind.
When thunder roars, go indoors.
Stay away from water and tall trees.
lessons.try: Make a thunderstorm safety card.

learn: Tornadoes are spinning columns of wind.
Go to a basement or inner room without windows.
Tornado warnings mean take shelter now.
check: During a tornado, go to a...
lessons.try: Practise a tornado drill.

learn: Hurricanes are huge storms that form over warm oceans.
They bring strong winds, rain and flooding.
People may evacuate (leave) before they hit.
lessons.try: Track a hurricane on a map.

learn: Floods happen when water overflows onto land.
Flash floods come fast after heavy rain, especially in deserts.
Turn around, don't drown: never drive or walk through flood water.
lessons.try: Make a flood safety poster.

learn: Droughts are long periods without rain.
Dry plants can catch fire easily.
Follow fire bans and report smoke.
check: A drought is a long time without...
lessons.try: Discuss how droughts lead to fires.

learn: Earthquakes shake the ground suddenly.
Drop, cover and hold on.
Stay away from windows.
check: During an earthquake, drop, cover and...
lessons.try: Practise drop, cover and hold on.

learn: Volcanoes erupt lava and ash.
Tsunamis are giant waves caused by undersea earthquakes.
Move to high ground if a tsunami warning sounds.
lessons.try: Map volcanoes and tsunami zones.

learn: Scientists watch weather and Earth to warn people.
Sirens, alerts on phones and radios give warnings.
Listen and act quickly.
lessons.try: Learn the warning signals in your town.

learn: Engineers design to reduce harm.
Earthquake-proof buildings sway. Levees hold back floods.
Lightning rods guide lightning safely to the ground.
check: Lightning rods guide lightning to the...
lessons.try: Design a model house that survives shaking.

learn: Every family needs a plan.
Know where to meet, who to call and what to pack.
An emergency kit has water, food, a torch and first aid.
lessons.try: Make an emergency kit checklist with your family.

learn: Natural hazards can't be stopped but can be prepared for.
Know the safety rules for each.
Engineers design to protect people.
check: For an earthquake: drop, cover and...
For a tornado, go to a...
lessons.try: Teach a hazard safety rule to a younger class.
